Q1.note: Umm al-Kitāb / al-Sabʿ al-Mathānī (Bukhārī 4474, 4703, 4474; Muslim 395). Recited 17×/day in salāh. The most-recited surah in human history.

Q112.note: Thuluth al-Qurʾān (Bukhārī 5013, 5014, 5015; Muslim 811, 812). Bukhārī dedicates a whole bāb. Recited in muʿawwidhāt routine; pre-sleep & morning/evening adhkār.

Q36.note: Qalb al-Qurʾān (Tirmidhī 2887; Aḥmad 5/26 — chain debated). Recited at deathbed (Abū Dāwūd 3121, Aḥmad). Mass-popular in funerary practice; >50 quoted citations across mosque sermons.

Q67.note: Surat al-Mulk = al-Munjiya / al-Wāqiya (intercedes for reciter, protects from grave-punishment): Tirmidhī 2891; Aḥmad; Abū Dāwūd 1400. Recited nightly per sunnah.

Q113.note: Muʿawwidha (Bukhārī 4976-4977; Muslim 814; Abū Dāwūd 1462; Tirmidhī 2902-2903). Daily morning/evening + post-salāh adhkār + last-thing-at-night triad.

Q114.note: Muʿawwidha (Bukhārī 4976-4977; Muslim 814; same daily liturgy as 113). Final-protection bracket.

Q2.note: al-Baqara — Bukhārī 5009, 5010 (last 2 verses suffice at night); Muslim 780, 808 (Shayṭān flees house with al-Baqara recitation); contains Āyat al-Kursī (Bukhārī 2311, Muslim 810: greatest verse in Qurʾān).

Q18.note: al-Kahf — Friday-recitation tradition (Ḥākim Mustadrak 2/399 #3392, Bayhaqī Shuʿab al-Īmān, graded ḥasan by Ibn Ḥajar). First/last 10 verses protect from Dajjāl (Muslim 809). Universally observed Friday-sunna.

Q55.note: al-Raḥmān — Tirmidhī 3291 (single chain): 'For everything there is a bride, the bride of the Qurʾān is Sūrat al-Raḥmān.' Chain debated (mursal). Liturgically recurrent but not mass-attested.

Q50.note: Qāf — Muslim 873; Abū Dāwūd 1102, 1123: Prophet recited Qāf during ʿīd and Friday khuṭba. Multiple chains.

Q87.note: al-Aʿlā — Muslim 878, Abū Dāwūd 1115, Nasāʾī: routine recitation in ʿīd, witr, jumuʿa second rakʿa. Also Aḥmad: Prophet loved this surah.

Q88.note: al-Ghāshiya — Muslim 878 (paired with al-Aʿlā in ʿīd & jumuʿa). Recurring liturgical use.

Q109.note: al-Kāfirūn — al-Tirmidhī 2893: equals quarter of Qurʾān. Muslim 726 (recited in fajr-sunna paired with Q112). Routine pre-sleep.

Q32.note: al-Sajda — Bukhārī 891, Muslim 880: Prophet recited Q32 + Q76 in fajr every Friday. Tirmidhī 2892 (chain debated): protects from grave-punishment if recited nightly.

Q76.note: al-Insān/al-Dahr — Bukhārī 891, Muslim 880: Friday fajr recitation alongside Q32.

Q17.note: Banū Isrāʾīl/al-Isrāʾ — Bukhārī 4708, 4709: Prophet recited al-Isrāʾ + Q39 + Q44 + others nightly before sleep ('al-musabbiḥāt' tradition; Tirmidhī 3406 chain debated).

Q57.note: al-Ḥadīd — al-musabbiḥāt cluster (Tirmidhī 2921, Abū Dāwūd 5057). Routine pre-sleep.

Q59.note: al-Ḥashr — last 3 verses (khawātim) recited morning/evening: Tirmidhī 2922, Abū Dāwūd 5079 (single chain, ḍaʿīf per most). Broadly practiced.

Q62.note: al-Jumuʿa — Muslim 877: recited in jumuʿa prayer. Routine liturgy.

Q63.note: al-Munāfiqūn — Muslim 877: paired with al-Jumuʿa in jumuʿa-second-rakʿa.

Q99.note: al-Zalzala — Tirmidhī 2893: equals half the Qurʾān (chain ḍaʿīf-ḥasan).

Q97.note: al-Qadr — Lailat al-Qadr veneration; Bukhārī 2014-2018 routinely cite this surah in laylat al-qadr context (theological framing).

Q3.note: Āl ʿImrān — Bukhārī 5009: paired with al-Baqara as 'al-Zahrāwān' (the two luminous ones) — intercede on Day of Judgment (Muslim 804).

Q9.note: al-Tawba — discussed in Bukhārī 4978, 4882, 4880 etc. for its no-basmala anomaly; theological-ḥarb context.

Q24.note: al-Nūr — Abū Dāwūd 1452 (Prophet ordered teaching Q24 to women); famous āyat al-nūr 24:35 separately venerated.

Q33.note: al-Aḥzāb — Bukhārī occasional citations on hijab/wives-of-prophet; not in fadāʾil-prominent list.

Q25.note: al-Furqān — occasional context citations; Bukhārī 4584 etc.

Q19.note: Maryam — Najashi-recitation hadith (Aḥmad, Ibn Hishām Sīra); recited at Habasha episode. Late-Meccan emotionally venerated.

Q20.note: Ṭāhā — pre-Hijra conversion narrative of ʿUmar (Ibn Hishām Sīra; cited in Suyūṭī Itqān).

Q12.note: Yūsuf — limited specific fadāʾil; thematic 'best of stories' (12:3 internal). Hadith mentions occasional.

Q23.note: al-Muʾminūn — Aḥmad, Tirmidhī: 10 verses opening recited for special reward (chain debated).

Q7.note: al-Aʿrāf — limited specific fadāʾil; Bukhārī 4729 occasional context.

Q6.note: al-Anʿām — Tirmidhī 3223 (chain ḍaʿīf): revealed with 70,000 angels. Limited mass-attestation.
